newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- small gains amid new supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- small gains amid new supply.

text.p: The U.S. municipal market gained about 1/8 to 1/4 point Tuesday in quiet action, market participants said.
Both the Treasury market and futures outperformed muni cash, as more than $1 billion in new issue pricings buffered the possibility of stronger gains.
Bear Stearns & Co repriced Tuesday's largest negotiated offering, a $269 million Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority deal. The bonds carried a top yield of 5.375 percent in 2024.

Prudential Securities won Tuesday's largest competitive offering, a $215 million Minnesota general obligation deal. The firm reoffered the 2017 maturity at a 5.15 percent yield. One market participant said a large unsold balance on the Minnesota deal was also keeping a lid on any late day gains in the secondary market.
Wednesday's new deals were expected to total $1.2 billion in 32 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

The negotiated total was $858 million, with the largest deal a $340 million issue expected from California Natural Resources through PaineWebber Inc. Maryland has claim to Wednesday's largest competitive deal, a $250 million general obligation issue at 1100 EDT.
The main data released Tuesday, the second quarter Employment Cost Index, showed an overall 0.8 percent rise, which was in line with the increase forecast by economists.
Treasury prices initially dipped after the data, but recovered in later trade. The long bond was up 8/32 at 103-5/32, pushing the yield down to 6.39 percent.

Despite that gain, analysts said investors were nervous about the next big indicator -- Friday's jobs report for July. Economist surveyed by Reuters on average expected non-farm payrolls to show a 193,000 gain, and the unemployment rate to have dropped to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent in June.

At the close Tuesday, September municipal bond futures rose 17/32 to 121-18/32, while Treasury bond futures gained 16/32 to 115-30/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 180 ticks from 179 at the close Monday.

Actively quoted bonds in the muni secondary market included Harris County, Texas, Toll Road MBIA 5.0s of 2024. Bids dropped five basis points to 5.28 percent late in the day, after trading two basis points lower at midday.
Florida Ports Financing Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 were bid at 5.48 percent, down one basis point from Monday.
